newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil sets goals for 1997/98 sugar crop plan.
newsitem.headline: Brazil sets goals for 1997/98 sugar crop plan.

text.p: Brazilian government officials and representatives from the private sugar sector discussed today the key goals of the 1997/98 sugar crop which is to begin in May, said a top government sugar official.
"The meeting today was to define the criteria of the crop plan," said Pedro Cabral, head of the Industry and Commerce Ministry's sugar and alcohol department.
"These are that we will not import any alcohol in 1997/98 and that we will produce enough alcohol to replace production of MTBE in Rio Grande do Sul and also some methanol," he added.
In 1996/97, Brazil imported around 400 million liters alcohol, Cabral said.
The next priority after meeting the needs of the domestic alcohol market is to meet its sugar needs.
Any remaining production will then be used for sugar exports, Cabral said.
States now have to submit their estimates of sugarcane production to the ministry by April 5, Cabral said.
"In 1996/97 we produced 290 million tonnes of cane. This year we hope it will be more," he added.
In order to meet the goals regarding no imports and replacement production of MTBE and methanol, one or two billion meters more of alcohol will need to be produced than in 1996/97, Cabral said.
"This is the first goal of the government," he said.
